mainEntity.name: Is it better to convert an existing room or build an addition for caregiver quarters?

acceptedAnswer.text: An interior room conversion reprograms existing square footage, such as an underused den or formal dining room, while an addition expands your home's footprint into the yard. Converting existing space usually moves faster and avoids major foundation work, but it reduces living area elsewhere in the house. Building a new addition provides total design freedom for accessible layouts, wider doorways, and independent plumbing, though it requires foundation construction, exterior framing, and exterior wall finishing like siding or stucco. Choosing between them depends on your available yard space, how quickly you need the suite ready, and whether you are willing to sacrifice existing interior rooms.
acceptedAnswer.description: An interior conversion repurposes existing interior rooms quickly, whereas a home addition builds new square footage outward without taking away from your current living areas.
